## Help Center: My Library

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/building-your-service/my-library

Your permanent, schedule-independent store of saved songs and slides.

**My Library** is your permanent, schedule-independent store of reusable content.

![My Library](/images/docs/07-my-library.webp)

## Two tabs

| Tab | Contains | How things get here |
|-----|----------|---------------------|
| **Songs** | Every song you've saved | **Add Song**, or the save icon on a song slide |
| **Slides** | Saved text, media, hymn, interlude and presentation slides | A slide's **⋮ → Save to Library** |

## What you can do

- **Search**: *"Search all saved songs / slides"* filters the current tab.
- **Add to the schedule**: click any item.
- **Edit**: via **⋮ → Edit** (songs open in the Add Song editor).
- **Delete**: via **⋮ → Delete**, with confirmation. Deleting from your library is **not reversible**.

A presentation can be saved once all of its pages have uploaded, so the saved copy opens on every device. Adding a saved presentation back to a schedule reuses those uploaded pages and does not use more cloud storage.

Empty states tell you what to do. With no saved songs you'll see *"No songs saved yet. Click the save icon on the Slide card to start saving."*

::callout{type="tip"}
Long lists load progressively as you scroll (15 at a time), so a large song library stays fast. You can also navigate the list with your keyboard.
::

## Related guides

- [Adding songs & hymns](/docs/building-your-service/adding-songs-and-hymns): save a song so it is ready every week.
- [Schedules](/docs/building-your-service/schedules): build the order of service from your library.
- [Song setlists](/docs/building-your-service/song-setlists): run several saved songs as one medley.

---

## Help Center: Song Setlists

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/building-your-service/song-setlists

Hold several songs in order on a single slide, so you can move through a worship medley without juggling separate slides.

A **Song Setlist** is a single slide holding **several songs in order**, so you can move through a worship medley without juggling separate slides.

![Song Setlist builder](/images/docs/08-song-setlist.webp)

## Creating one

1. Click **Song Setlist**. A new setlist slide is created, reading *"Add songs to this setlist from the song list."*
2. Add songs (below).
3. The card title tracks its contents: **"Song Setlist 1 (0 songs)"** → **"(3 songs)"**.

## Adding songs

- **Drag a song slide** from the Slide Schedule Pane **onto the setlist slide**, or
- Add songs from the song list or My Library while the setlist is selected.

## Reordering songs

The songs in a setlist appear as cards across the top of the Preview & Edit Pane. Drag a card to move that song. The song that is showing stays active wherever you move it, and each song keeps its place in its own verses. Click a card to jump to that song, or use its trash icon to remove it.

## Running a setlist live

The setlist tracks two positions at once: **which song** is active, and **which verse** of that song is showing. **←** and **→** move through verses, rolling into the next song at the end. The slide title updates to the current verse (for example "Verse 2").

## Setlist vs. individual song slides

| | Individual song slides | Song Setlist |
|---|---|---|
| Slides in schedule | One per song | One for the whole set |
| Reordering mid-service | Move slides around | Reorder within the setlist |
| Best for | A song at one point in the service | A back-to-back worship medley |

## Related guides

- [Adding songs & hymns](/docs/building-your-service/adding-songs-and-hymns): add the songs a setlist is built from.
- [Promoting slides](/docs/going-live/promoting-slides): the arrow keys for moving through verses live.
- [Stage display](/docs/going-live/stage-display): show the band what is next.

---

# Help Center: Going Live

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/going-live

Open the live display, promote slides, set up a second screen, use the stage display, blank the screen, and send alerts or a livestream feed.

How to get your slides onto the projector and keep the service running smoothly. Open the Live Display, put slides on screen with a click or the arrow keys, and set up a second screen or a stage display for your musicians and preacher. When you need to, blank the screen, send an alert over the slide, or send the output to your livestream in OBS or vMix, or over NDI.

Setting up for the first time? Start with [Opening the live display](/docs/going-live/opening-the-live-display) and [Multi-screen setup](/docs/going-live/multi-screen-setup).

---

## Help Center: Opening the Live Display

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/going-live/opening-the-live-display

Go Live opens the projection window. Drag it to your projector, go fullscreen, and you're ready to promote slides.

Click **Go Live** in the Slide Schedule Pane header. It opens a small menu:

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| **Open live window** | Opens another browser window with the live display. Drag this to your projector |
| **Open stage display** | Opens the confidence monitor for musicians and speakers. Teams, see [Stage Display](/docs/going-live/stage-display) |
| **Copy livestream link** | A link for OBS, vMix or similar software. Free churches get 5 sessions, see [Livestream output](/docs/going-live/livestream-output-obs-vmix) |
| **Copy stage display link** | Opens the stage display on any phone, tablet or TV. Teams, see [Stage Display](/docs/going-live/stage-display#on-a-phone-tablet-or-tv) |

::callout{type="important" title="Go Live opens the window, not a slide"}
**Go Live** opens the output *window*. It does not by itself put a slide on screen. Once the window is open, the button becomes **End Live Session**. To show something, [promote a slide](/docs/going-live/promoting-slides).
::

![Live projection output](/images/docs/14-live-projection.webp)

## Going fullscreen

A banner reads *"Double click the display below to toggle full screen and remove this banner."* Do exactly that, or press **F** with the live window focused.

::callout{type="tip" title="Skip this step every week"}
Turn on **Settings → Display Settings → Open in fullscreen mode** so the live window always opens fullscreen.
::

## Keeping the live window alive

By default the live window is independent of the Control Center tab. If **Settings → Display Settings → "Close live window when this tab is closed"** is on, closing the Control Center also closes the projection. Leave it **off** if you want the projection to survive a Control Center reload. See [Multi-screen setup](/docs/going-live/multi-screen-setup).

---

## Help Center: Promoting Slides

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/going-live/promoting-slides

Three ways to put a slide on screen, and the arrow keys that make running a service fast.

Three ways to put a slide on screen:

1. **Click the slide** in the Slide Schedule Pane.
2. Click **Go Live** inside the slide's editor.
3. Keyboard: **Cmd/Ctrl + P** for the slide in the editor, or **Cmd/Ctrl + [number]** by position.

![A slide live with the LIVE badge](/images/docs/13-go-live-active.webp)

The live slide is marked **LIVE** in both the Slide Schedule Pane and the Live Output Preview. Clicking a different slide switches instantly.

::callout{type="tip" title="The fastest way to run a service"}
**↑** and **↓** move to the previous or next slide in the schedule and promote it. Once your order is set, you can run the whole service from the arrow keys.
::

## Schedule shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| **↓** | Send the next slide in the schedule live |
| **↑** | Send the previous slide in the schedule live |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + 1…9** | Send that numbered slide live |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + 0** | Send the last slide in the schedule live |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + P** | Promote the slide you're previewing |
| **B** | Blank the live output |

Inside a scripture, song or hymn slide, **←** and **→** move between verses.

## Related guides

- [Opening the live display](/docs/going-live/opening-the-live-display): open the projection window first.
- [Blank screen](/docs/going-live/blank-screen): clear the screen between segments.
- [Keyboard shortcuts](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/keyboard-shortcuts): every shortcut, including the live ones.
- [Using Cloud of Worship on your phone](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/using-cloud-of-worship-on-your-phone): drive the projector from your phone.

---

## Help Center: Multi-Screen Setup

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/going-live/multi-screen-setup

Assign your projector as the Live display and a second monitor as the Stage display from Display Settings.

**Settings → Display Settings** handles projector setup.

## Control Center

Shows the screen you're operating on, its resolution, and whether it's your primary screen, with the advice: *"This is where behind the scene control is done. We advise you get a second screen for the live content."*

If the Control Center has ended up on the wrong monitor, click **Move to primary screen**.

## Live Window Settings

| Setting | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Open in fullscreen mode** | Live window opens fullscreen automatically |
| **Close live window when this tab is closed** | Ties the live window's lifetime to the Control Center tab or window. Leave this **off** if you want the projection to survive a Control Center reload. |
| **Let a team member's phone control this output** | On by default. Lets someone on a phone pick this device and take slides live on the screen it is driving, but only while the live window is open here. Stored on this computer only. See [using CoW on your phone](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/using-cloud-of-worship-on-your-phone) |

## Secondary Screens

CoW detects connected monitors and lists each with its label and resolution. Each screen can be assigned one of two roles:

- Toggle **Live display** on the screen you want to project the service to.
- Toggle **Stage display** on a screen facing your musicians and speakers (Teams). See [Stage display](/docs/going-live/stage-display).

A screen can only hold one role at a time. Turning **Live display** on for a screen already assigned as the stage display releases it from that role first (and vice versa).

- **Refresh screens** re-detects monitors if you plugged one in after loading.
- **"No external screens detected"** means only one display is connected, or your browser hasn't granted screen-detection permission. Chrome and Edge support this best.
- With only one external screen connected, you can still assign the **stage display**. It just opens in a new browser tab instead of on its own monitor.

::callout{type="tip" title="Detection is browser-dependent"}
Automatic screen detection works best in Chrome and Edge. In other browsers you may see **"No external screens detected"** and will need to drag the live window to your projector manually, which works fine.
::

::callout{type="tip" title="The desktop app skips all of this"}
On the [Windows desktop app](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/desktop-app), monitors are read from the operating system rather than the browser, so there is no permission prompt and no *"No external screens detected"*. The live and stage displays open as real application windows placed directly on the monitor you choose, with no popup blocker involved.
::

---

## Help Center: Stage Display

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/going-live/stage-display

A confidence monitor for musicians and speakers with live and next content, a service stopwatch, a private countdown and the clock.

*Teams feature.*

The Stage Display is a confidence monitor for musicians, vocalists and speakers. It shows what's live, what's coming next, a timer and the time of day, without the Control Center's slide editing tools. On the Starter plan, opening it shows an upgrade screen instead.

## Opening it

Open it with the **Open Stage Display** quick action, or by assigning a monitor to it in **Settings → Display Settings**. See [Multi-screen setup](/docs/going-live/multi-screen-setup).

## On a phone, tablet or TV

Click **Go Live → Copy stage display link** and open the link on any device with a browser. The link ends in the schedule's 6-character code. If you'd rather type it, open `/stagestream`, enter the code on the **Open the stage display** screen and the same board opens. It shows the same Now, Next and timer panels as the Stage Display, and the layout adapts to phones held either way up.

The link only ever shows what's live and what's next. It carries no schedule or Bible data, so it is safe to send to the band's group chat. It updates only while the presentation computer is running the service, and it shows a connection status when it is reconnecting. The timer on the link is read-only: start, pause and reset stay on the presentation computer.

## Slide pictures and a closed console

When the live or next slide is a presentation page or an image, the Now and Next panels show the picture, fitted edge to edge, on the Stage Display and on the stage display link. Video slides still show a placeholder.

If the Control Center is closed or crashes, the Stage Display shows a warning row instead of leaving stale words on screen as if they were live. Reopen the Control Center and it carries on.

## Four panels

| Panel | Shows |
|-------|-------|
| **Now** | The text of whatever slide is currently live |
| **Next** | The text of the upcoming slide in the schedule |
| **Timer** | A stage-only countdown when one is loaded, otherwise the live countdown slide or the service stopwatch. Stage-owned clocks have start, pause and reset controls. A countdown turns **red** at zero. |
| **Clock** | The current time |

The text in **Now** and **Next** resizes itself to fill the space available, so a short line is large and a long verse still fits without scrolling. On a narrow or portrait screen the panels stack vertically instead of the normal 2-column grid, so a TV mounted in portrait works well.

## Choose what the timer panel shows

The panel follows this order:

1. **Stage countdown:** A private countdown the operator starts for the band or speaker. It stays on the Stage Display and does not add a slide to the schedule or change the congregation's screen.
2. **Live countdown:** If a countdown slide is live and there is no stage countdown, the panel mirrors its remaining time. Its controls stay with the live slide, so the Stage Display has no start or reset buttons for it.
3. **Service stopwatch:** At other times, the panel counts up. Search Quick Actions for **Start Stage Clock**, **Pause Stage Clock** or **Restart Stage Clock**. The buttons on the Stage Display control this same clock.

To start a private countdown, search for **Stage Display Countdown** in Quick Actions. Choose the **Stage Display** tab, set a duration, optionally add text beneath the timer, then click **Start stage countdown**. Typing a duration such as *5 min countdown* also offers an instant stage action. See [Countdown timers](/docs/building-your-service/countdown-timers) for both destinations.

The service stopwatch continues underneath a stage countdown. Search for **Clear Stage Countdown** to return to its current reading. A stage countdown remains at zero until you clear or restart it.

For a practical example, read [How to run a Stage Display countdown without changing the live screen](/blog/how-to-run-a-stage-display-countdown-without-changing-the-live-screen).

Like the Live Display, double-click anywhere on the Stage Display to toggle full screen (or press **F**). This also removes the banner reminding you it's the stage display.

::callout{type="tip" title="Safe to hand off"}
Nothing on the Stage Display can edit a slide or take one live. Its start, pause and reset buttons control the service stopwatch or stage countdown, whichever is showing. They are hidden while it mirrors a live countdown slide.
::

## Alerts and overlays do not appear here

[Alerts and overlays](/docs/going-live/alerts-and-overlays) reach the congregation's screen and the livestream, and are deliberately kept off the Stage Display. The band does not need the car park announcement covering their lyrics.

## It runs from the operator's computer

The Stage Display window is fed directly by the Control Center on the same machine, so plug the stage screen into the presentation computer. You can run more than one from that computer, for example one for the worship team and one for the preacher. For a screen that isn't plugged in, use the [stage display link](#on-a-phone-tablet-or-tv) instead.

Stage clock actions are available on that computer, not from a phone. Controlling live slides from a separate device is a different job. See [using CoW on your phone](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/using-cloud-of-worship-on-your-phone).

---

## Help Center: Blank Screen

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/going-live/blank-screen

Clear the Live Display between segments, during prayer or while you set up. Formerly called Intermission.

::callout{type="important" title="Formerly Intermission"}
This was called **Intermission** in earlier versions of CoW. The feature and the shortcut key are the same. Only the name, and the default idle screen, changed.
::

**Blank** clears the Live Display. Click **Blank** in the Slide Schedule Pane header, or press **B**, whenever the screen should rest: between segments, during prayer, or while you set up.

![Blank idle live screen](/images/docs/15-intermission-live.webp)

## What shows while blank

By default the screen goes **completely black**. There's no more automatic church-branding (logo and name) screen. If you want something other than black while idle, set a custom **video or image** background in **Settings → Blank Settings** (**Use a video / image background**).

::callout{type="warning" title="Blank is not a toggle"}
It clears the live slide and does not remember what was there. To resume, click the slide you want. The button is **disabled while nothing is live**.
::

## Related guides

- [Promoting slides](/docs/going-live/promoting-slides): put a slide back on screen after blanking.
- [Interlude slides](/docs/building-your-service/interlude-slides): an animated break screen instead of black.
- [Settings reference](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/settings-reference): Blank Settings and the idle background.
- [Live display problems](/docs/troubleshooting/live-display-problems): a black screen you did not ask for.

---

## Help Center: Alerts & Overlays

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/going-live/alerts-and-overlays

Put a scrolling alert or a lower-third overlay on screen without disturbing the slide underneath. Teams features.

Sometimes you need to tell the room something without taking the lyrics or the sermon point off the screen: a parent needed at the children's church, a car blocking the gate, a reminder about the next event. Alerts and overlays sit **on top of** the live slide, so the service carries on underneath.

| | Alert | Overlay |
|---|-------|---------|
| **Looks like** | A coloured banner that scrolls across the top or bottom | A text or countdown box placed anywhere on screen, like a lower-third |
| **Made from** | The **Add Banners/Alert** panel | An existing text or countdown slide |
| **Best for** | Short, urgent notices | Speaker names, a countdown to the next segment, a standing reminder |
| **Plan** | Teams | Teams |

Free churches can open the alert panel to try it; sending an alert live needs [Teams](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/plans-free-vs-teams).

## Alerts (Teams)

![Alert configuration](/images/docs/12-add-banner-alert.webp)

### Send an alert

1. Click **Add Banners/Alert** in the [Quick Actions Pane](/docs/control-center/quick-actions-pane).
2. Pick a **Banner color**.
3. Choose an **Alert position**: **Top** or **Bottom**.
4. Type **Your alert content**.
5. Set the scroll **Speed** with the slider, from **Slow** to **Fast**.
6. Click **Send alert to LIVE**.

The alert scrolls across the [Live Display](/docs/going-live/opening-the-live-display) over whatever slide is showing.

### The alert schedule

Alerts you've sent are kept in an **Alert schedule** at the top of the panel, so you can send the same notice again with one click instead of retyping it. Only one alert is live at a time, marked with the live dot. The counter shows how many you've saved out of your limit, which you can change from 5 to 30 in **Settings → Other Settings → Default alert limit** (5 by default).

### Remove an alert

Search for **Remove Alert** in the Quick Actions Pane to clear the banner in one click.

## Overlays (Teams)

An **overlay** shows a slide *on top of* the current live slide instead of replacing it. Use it for lower-thirds such as a speaker's name, a giving reminder, or a countdown to the next part of the service.

### Make an overlay

Overlays are made from **text slides** (with the full-text or heading-and-subtitle layout) and **countdown slides**.

1. Create the slide first. See [Text slides](/docs/building-your-service/text-slides) or [Countdown timers](/docs/building-your-service/countdown-timers).
2. Open the slide's **⋮** menu and choose **Duplicate as Overlay**.

### Show and clear an overlay

- **Double-click** the overlay slide in your schedule to show it, or select it and click **Show Overlay**.
- Click the overlay in the live preview, or **Clear Overlay**, to take it off.

### Overlay settings

In **Settings → Other Settings**:

- **Position**: top left, top middle, top right, middle, bottom left, bottom middle or bottom right.
- **Size** of the overlay box.
- **Decorative overlay**: an optional seasonal effect, such as **Falling Snow**.

::callout{type="tip" title="Livestreaming?"}
Alerts and overlays are part of the live output, so they also appear in [OBS or vMix](/docs/going-live/livestream-output-obs-vmix). Keep alerts meant only for the room short, or clear them before a stream segment.
::

---

## Help Center: Livestream Output (OBS / vMix)

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/going-live/livestream-output-obs-vmix

Feed your live slides into OBS, vMix or similar software as a browser source, so your online congregation sees the same lyrics and scripture as the room.

*Unlimited on Teams. Free churches get 5 sessions.*

Beyond the projector, CoW can feed your **online stream**. Click **Go Live → Copy livestream link**. You'll get a toast confirming *"Livestream URL copied to clipboard."*

## On the Free plan

Each church on Free gets **5 livestream sessions**. Streaming a schedule on a new day uses one, so a Sunday service and a midweek service are two sessions. The **Go Live** menu shows how many are left, for example *"3 of 5 free sessions left"*. Once they are used, the link shows an upgrade message instead of your slides. See [Plans](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/plans-free-vs-teams#free-allowances).

## Using the URL

The copied URL points at a dedicated, schedule-specific viewer page. Add it as a **Browser Source** in OBS, vMix or similar software and it will follow your live slides automatically, so your online congregation sees the same lyrics and scripture as the room.

It shows a **connection status indicator** when connecting or disconnected, and displays a loading progress screen while it pulls down the schedule's resources on first open.

::callout{type="important" title="The URL is per schedule"}
The URL is tied to the **currently active schedule**. If you switch schedules, copy a fresh URL.
::

## The schedule code

The copied link ends in the schedule's **6-character code**, for example `/livestream/AB12CD`. The code also shows on each schedule row in the schedule list, before *Created*. Anyone can open `/livestream` on its own and type the code into the **Watch the livestream** screen. It tells you if the code is unknown, if there were too many attempts, or if CoW can't be reached. Older links that use the long schedule ID keep working.

## Step-by-step guides

- [Using Cloud of Worship with OBS](/blog/how-to-use-cloud-of-worship-with-obs-livestream)
- [Using Cloud of Worship with vMix](/blog/how-to-use-cloud-of-worship-with-vmix-livestream)

---

## Help Center: NDI Live Output

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/going-live/ndi-output

Publish the live display as an NDI source on your local network, so OBS, vMix, TriCaster or any NDI receiver can pick up your slides without a capture card.

*Free feature. Desktop app only.*

NDI sends your live display over the local network as a video source. Any NDI receiver on the same network (OBS, vMix, TriCaster, an NDI-capable switcher or monitor) can pick it up and use it like a camera input, with no capture card and no cable between machines.

::callout{type="important" title="This is the desktop app only"}
The NDI section appears in **Settings → Display Settings** only when you are running the installed [desktop app](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/desktop-app). In the browser, use the [livestream URL](/docs/going-live/livestream-output-obs-vmix) as a browser source instead.

The desktop app currently ships for **Windows** only, so NDI output is a Windows feature today. The macOS notes below apply to the macOS build once it is released.
::

## Before you start

1. **Install the NDI runtime.** It is not bundled with Cloud of Worship. Install **NDI Tools** or the NDI runtime from [ndi.video/tools](https://ndi.video/tools/). NDI 5 and NDI 6 are both supported, and NDI 6 is preferred when both are present.
2. **Use one network.** The sending computer and the receiving computer must be on the same local network. NDI discovery does not cross the public internet.
3. **On Windows**, you need Windows 10 version 1903 or newer.

## Turning it on

1. Open **Settings → Display Settings → NDI Live Output**.
2. Switch on **Broadcast live output over NDI**.
3. Open the live display. Broadcasting starts as soon as the live window opens, and stops when you close it.

If the live window is not open yet when you flip the toggle, you will see *"NDI will start with the live window"*. That is expected. Open the live display and it begins on its own.

In your receiver, look for a source named **CoW Live Output** on the sending computer.

::callout{type="tip" title="The preference stays on this machine"}
**Broadcast live output over NDI** is stored on that computer only. It never syncs to your account or to your teammates, so turning it on at the church laptop will not turn it on for someone at home.
::

## What the output looks like

| | |
|---|---|
| **Source name** | CoW Live Output |
| **Resolution** | Matches the live window, scaled down to fit 1920 x 1080 |
| **Frame rate** | 30 fps |
| **Cursor** | Not included |

The feed is exactly what the live display shows, so blank screen, alerts, backgrounds and overlays all come through.

## Reading the status panel

The panel under the toggle is the honest state of the broadcast.

| Row | What it means |
|-----|---------------|
| **Status** (with the coloured dot) | *Not broadcasting*, *Starting*, *Broadcasting*, *Needs attention*, or *Unsupported on this system* |
| **Source** | The name receivers will see. Always CoW Live Output |
| **Resolution** | The captured size and frame rate, or *Waiting for live output* before the first frame arrives |
| **NDI runtime** | The runtime version that was found and loaded, or *Not detected*. Hover it to see the file it loaded from |
| **Receivers** | How many receivers are currently pulling the source right now |

### "Broadcasting last frame" with an amber Stalled badge

This means the sender is healthy and still feeding receivers at 30 fps, but the live window has not produced a new frame in the last 2 seconds, so it is repeating the last one.

This is normal and harmless most of the time. Screen capture only produces a frame when something on the live display actually changes, so a still slide with no video or animation legitimately produces nothing new. The badge clears by itself the moment you change slide or play a video. On Windows it also appears when the live window is minimized.

Worry about it only when the badge stays on while something is visibly moving on the live display. That points at capture having stopped, and the status usually turns to **Needs attention** with an error in the same panel.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | What to do |
|--------------|------------|
| *The NDI runtime is not installed or could not be found* | Install NDI Tools or the runtime from [ndi.video/tools](https://ndi.video/tools/), then press **Retry**. The **Install NDI runtime** button in the panel opens the same page |
| *The installed NDI runtime could not be loaded* / *does not export…* | The runtime is present but broken or too old. Update or reinstall it, then press **Retry** |
| *Open the live output window before starting NDI* | The live display is closed. Open it and broadcasting starts on its own |
| *Screen Recording permission is required…* (macOS 14.3 and older) | Press **Open Screen Recording settings**, enable Cloud of Worship under **Privacy & Security → Screen Recording**, then restart the app. macOS 14.4 and newer does not need this |
| *ScreenCaptureKit could not uniquely identify the live output window* | Close duplicate Cloud of Worship windows, then press **Retry** |
| *NDI live output requires Windows 10 version 1903 or newer* | Update Windows |
| *This computer's CPU is not supported…* | The NDI runtime cannot run on that processor. There is no workaround on that machine |
| **Broadcasting** but **Receivers: 0** | The receiver cannot discover the source. See below |

### The receiver cannot find CoW Live Output

- Confirm both machines are on the **same network**, and that it is not a guest network that isolates clients from each other.
- On Windows, allow **Cloud of Worship** through Windows Firewall, and make sure the network is set to **Private** rather than Public. The app shows this hint in the panel when nothing has connected.
- Some networks block the multicast and mDNS traffic NDI uses for discovery. If yours does, add the sending computer manually in **NDI Access Manager** as a remote source.
- Wired ethernet is strongly preferred. 1080p30 NDI is a heavy stream, and congested WiFi shows up as stutter or dropouts at the receiver.

::callout{type="warning" title="NDI is not a substitute for the projector output"}
Use NDI to feed your stream or a switcher. Keep projecting to the physical screen through [multi-screen setup](/docs/going-live/multi-screen-setup). If NDI stops, the room still sees the slides.
::

## NDI or the livestream URL?

Both feed your stream, and they solve different problems.

| | NDI | [Livestream URL](/docs/going-live/livestream-output-obs-vmix) |
|---|---|---|
| **Where it runs** | Desktop app only (Windows today) | Any browser, any machine |
| **Needs** | NDI runtime, same local network | An internet connection |
| **Carries** | The live display exactly as rendered, as video | The slides, rendered again in the receiving browser |
| **Best for** | A switcher or an OBS machine in the same building | A remote stream operator, or when installing anything is not an option |
| **Plan** | Free | Teams |

---

# Help Center: Teams & Collaboration

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/teams-and-collaboration

Invite your media team, work together in real time, transcribe sermons, and compare the Free and Teams plans.

Cloud of Worship is built for church media teams. Invite your volunteers to the same church, prepare slides together in real time from different computers, and control the projector from a phone at the media desk. This section also covers live sermon transcription and what the Free and Teams plans include.

To bring your team in, start with [Working as a team](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/working-as-a-team).

---

## Help Center: Working as a Team

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/teams-and-collaboration/working-as-a-team

CoW is real-time collaborative. Invite teammates, see what syncs live, and understand slide locking.

CoW is real-time collaborative. Everyone signed into the same church works on the same schedules, and changes appear on each other's screens as they are made.

## Inviting people

Click **Invite** in the top bar. You can:

- Enter **email addresses** (comma-separated) and click **Send Invite**, or
- Click **Copy invite link** to share a join link. It changes to **"Copied!"** to confirm.

Existing members are listed with their role, **Admin** or **Member**. The person who created the church is the Admin.

Invitees land on the [dedicated join page](/docs/getting-started/joining-an-existing-church).

::callout{type="important"}
**Invite to Workspace** is a Teams feature. See [Plans: Free vs Teams](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/plans-free-vs-teams).
::

## What syncs live

- Slide create, update and delete, including batch changes
- Online presence: who else is in the workspace
- Alerts and overlays

When a teammate adds or deletes slides, you get a short notice naming them, for example *"Amazing Grace" and "John 3:16"* or *"Amazing Grace" and 4 other slides*, so you can see what changed without hunting for it.

## What does not sync: the live output

Taking a slide live is **local to the device that owns the live window**. It does not move anyone else's live display, and a teammate at home clicking a slide will not change what your congregation is looking at.

That is deliberate. An earlier version synced the live slide across every client, which meant any window open on the schedule could move the congregation screen, with no way to say which screen a change was meant for.

There are two ways a slide reaches a screen other than your own:

- **[Livestream viewers](/docs/going-live/livestream-output-obs-vmix)** follow the device that owns the live window, one way.
- **A phone can drive one named output**, chosen explicitly, and only while that computer has its live window open and has left the setting on. See [using CoW on your phone](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/using-cloud-of-worship-on-your-phone).

## Phones are full team members

On a Teams plan, someone on a phone is a full operator, not a viewer. They can build slides, switch schedules and, if you let them, take slides live on the projector at the media desk. See [using CoW on your phone](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/using-cloud-of-worship-on-your-phone).

## Slide locking

When someone is editing a slide, CoW locks it so two operators can't overwrite each other. If a slide is locked you'll be told rather than silently losing your change.

::callout{type="tip" title="Changes not showing up?"}
Check for the offline banner. If you're online, run **Refresh Slides** to re-fetch from the server. More in [Sync & team problems](/docs/troubleshooting/sync-and-team-problems).
::

---

## Help Center: Sermon Transcription

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/teams-and-collaboration/sermon-transcription

Turn your microphone into a live note-taker that surfaces relevant Bible passages automatically as you preach. A Teams feature.

*Teams feature, with 10 free minutes on Free.* Open with **Transcribe Sermon**.

> *"Transcribe Sermon turns your microphone into a live note-taker; capturing what's being said and surfacing relevant Bible passages automatically as you preach."*

## Three things it does

| Capability | What happens |
|-----------|--------------|
| **Live transcription** | Words appear in real time as you speak, with Bible references highlighted |
| **Auto-detect scriptures** | Any verse mentioned (for example "John 3:16") is instantly added to the **Scriptures** tab. Click it to open the slide |
| **AI scripture suggestions** | Related verses surface even when you don't quote them directly |

The panel has two tabs, **Transcripts** and **Scriptures**. Before anything is detected the Scriptures tab reads *"Scriptures matching the sermon will appear here automatically."*

## How much you can transcribe

Teams includes **3 hours of transcription every week**, and the limit resets every Monday. Minutes you don't use roll over into the next week, so a quiet week leaves you up to 6 hours for the one after. Rollover only carries one week: minutes that were rolled over don't roll again. A church on Free gets **10 minutes** once, to try it on a real sermon. The panel shows how many free minutes are left, and the timer turns amber when you're close to the end. Once the free minutes are used, transcription is part of Teams.

## Setup

Choose your input in **Settings → Microphone Settings**, which lists **Available Microphones** and lets you mark one **Use as default**. If the browser blocks access you'll see **"Microphone access denied"**. Grant mic permission in your browser's site settings.

## Related toggles

In **Settings → Other Settings**:

- **Automatic transcription actions**
- **Voice Bible version changes**: switch translation by voice

::callout{type="tip"}
Read the full walkthrough: [How to use sermon transcription and voice commands](/blog/how-to-use-sermon-transcription-and-voice-commands-in-cloud-of-worship).
::

## Related guides

- [Adding scripture](/docs/building-your-service/adding-scripture): put a suggested passage on screen.
- [Settings reference](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/settings-reference): microphone and transcription settings.
- [Media & transcription problems](/docs/troubleshooting/media-and-transcription-problems): microphone access denied and minutes used up.
- [Plans: Free vs Teams](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/plans-free-vs-teams): what each plan includes.

## Help Center: Plans: Free vs Teams

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/teams-and-collaboration/plans-free-vs-teams

What's included on the Free plan, what Teams unlocks, and how your plan is tied to your church.

| | Free | Teams |
|---|------|-------|
| Bible, hymns, songs, setlists, text, media slides | ✅ | ✅ |
| Schedules and My Library | ✅ | ✅ |
| PDF import | ✅ | ✅ |
| Dark mode, shortcuts, all settings | ✅ | ✅ |
| Desktop app and NDI output | ✅ | ✅ |
| Offline use and Bible downloads | ✅ | ✅ |
| **Search song lyrics** | 50 songs a month | Unlimited |
| **Slide Templates** | — | ✅ |
| **Alerts / banners** | — | ✅ |
| **Overlays** | — | ✅ |
| **Countdown timers** | — | ✅ |
| **Time slides** | — | ✅ |
| **Interlude slides** | — | ✅ |
| **Slide pairs** | — | ✅ |
| **YouTube / Vimeo embeds** | — | ✅ |
| **Sermon transcription** | 10 minutes, once | 3 hours a week, unused minutes roll over a week |
| **Inviting teammates** | — | ✅ |
| **Livestream URL (OBS / vMix)** | 5 sessions | Unlimited |
| **Stage Display and stage display link** | — | ✅ |
| **Using CoW on a phone** | — | ✅ |
| **Cloud storage** | 100 MB | 5 GB |
| **Background image upload** | 3 MB | 10 MB |
| **Background video upload** | 250 MB | Unlimited |

## Trying Teams features on Free

Many Teams features open on the Free plan so you can see what you'd get before paying. Slide Templates, alerts, countdowns, interludes and YouTube or Vimeo embeds all open their panel as normal, with a small Teams notice at the top. Fill the panel in as you like. The upgrade prompt only appears when you click the final **Create**, **Add** or **Send** button.

One-click actions with nothing to preview, such as time slides, removing an alert and the stage clock controls, show the upgrade prompt straight away.

## Free allowances

Three features are metered on Free rather than locked, so you can use them for real:

| Feature | Free allowance | How it's counted |
|---------|----------------|------------------|
| **Search song lyrics** | 50 songs a month | Search is free. Adding a song from the results to your schedule uses one. The count resets at midnight UTC on the 1st of each month. |
| **Sermon transcription** | 10 minutes | A one-off allowance per church. The panel shows how many free minutes are left. |
| **Livestream URL** | 5 sessions | Streaming a schedule on a new day uses one session. The **Go Live** menu shows how many are left. |

When an allowance runs out, the feature shows the upgrade prompt. Allowances belong to the church, so every member draws from the same count.

::callout{type="important" title="Your plan comes from your church"}
Your plan comes from your **church** record, not your personal user record. When an admin upgrades the church, every member gets Teams features.
::

::callout{type="warning" title="Expiry heads-up"}
If your Teams subscription is within **7 days of expiring**, a banner appears across the top of the Control Center.
::

## If your Teams plan lapses

Slides you made with a Teams feature stay in your schedule. They just can't be taken live until Teams returns, and CoW shows the upgrade prompt if you try. Nothing is deleted, so renewing brings everything back.

## If a payment fails

If your latest Teams payment doesn't go through, a red banner appears in **App Settings → Subscription Settings** with two buttons:

- **Retry payment** tries the charge again. A decline shows the bank's reason. If the charge is still pending, CoW checks until it clears and Teams returns by itself. If your bank needs you to confirm, its confirmation page opens.
- **Update payment method** lets you switch to a different card.

For the first 3 days the banner tells you when Teams features switch off. After that it tells you until when the payment can still be fixed. **Update payment method** also sits next to **Cancel Subscription**, so you can change your card at any time. If you click a Teams feature while a payment is overdue, the upgrade prompt sends you to fix the payment instead of starting a second subscription. Once the payment clears, Teams features unlock straight away.

## Upgrading

Use the **Upgrade Plan** quick action, or go to **App Settings → Subscription Settings**. Current prices are on the [pricing page](/pricing).

- [Quick Actions reference](/docs/control-center/quick-actions-reference): every action and the plan it needs.
- [Working as a team](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/working-as-a-team): invite your media team.
- [Sermon transcription](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/sermon-transcription): transcription minutes on each plan.
- [Account & sign-in problems](/docs/troubleshooting/account-and-sign-in-problems): Teams features greyed out after upgrading.

## Help Center: Using Cloud of Worship on Your Phone

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/teams-and-collaboration/using-cloud-of-worship-on-your-phone

Build slides, switch schedules and drive the projector at the media desk from a phone, without taking over anyone else's screen.

*Teams feature.*

Open `app.cloudofworship.com` on a phone and you get a full operator, laid out for a small screen. Not a viewer, not a remote with three buttons: the same Control Center, the same Quick Actions, the same schedule.

This is for the moments that do not happen at the media desk. The pastor changes the closing song. A scripture is needed that was not in the plan. The person who knows the software is currently leading worship.

## The layout

The phone opens on the **slide grid**, which is your schedule. Tapping a slide selects it, exactly as on desktop. Three buttons along the bottom bring up the rest, one at a time, and tapping the button you are already on returns you to the grid.

| Tab | What it is |
|-----|------------|
| **Quick Actions** | The desktop left column, given the whole screen: Bible, songs, hymns, media, My Library, templates, countdown slides, PDF import |
| **Live** | The live preview, the slide schedule under it, and the live output menu |
| **Schedules** | Switching which service you are working on |

Anything you create on the phone reaches the rest of your team instantly, and their slides reach you. A phone is a full member of the schedule. See [working as a team](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/working-as-a-team).

The phone can create a countdown slide for the congregation. It does not offer [Stage Display](/docs/going-live/stage-display) clock controls, which work on the presentation computer connected to that screen.

## Driving the projector from a phone

Creating slides is one thing. Changing what the congregation is looking at is another, and Cloud of Worship is deliberately careful here.

A phone does not broadcast to every screen in the building. It picks **one specific output** and drives that one. In a room where several laptops have the schedule open, a change made from a phone lands on the projector and nowhere else.

### On the computer driving the projector

1. **Open the live window.** A device only offers itself for control while its live window is actually open. A laptop merely viewing the schedule is not an output.
2. Open **Settings → Display Settings**.
3. Check that **Let a team member's phone control this output** is on. It is on by default, and it is stored on that computer only, so switching it off at the media desk changes nothing for anyone else.

### On the phone

At the top of the **Live** tab there is a status row telling you exactly where your slides are going:

| What it says | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Not controlling a screen** | Slides you take live only reach the livestream. Tap the row to pick an output |
| **Controlling [name]'s screen** | You are driving that device's live output. The device name is shown underneath |
| **Reconnecting to the output…** | That screen dropped off. Slides are paused until it comes back |

Tap the row, choose a screen from the list, and tap slides to take them live. If no computer in your team has a live window open, the list says **No output device online**.

The phone's preview mirrors what that projector is actually showing, not what the phone last asked for, so you can see whether your change landed.

::callout{type="important" title="Nobody is taken over quietly"}
Back at the media desk, the operator sees who is currently controlling the output above the slide schedule, and that indicator clears once the phone has been idle for a couple of minutes. Control itself ends when the live window on the host computer closes, or when the operator switches the setting off.
::

## The computer stays in charge

The device with the projector attached remains responsible for its own screen, and it is the device that keeps feeding [livestream viewers](/docs/going-live/livestream-output-obs-vmix). A phone borrows control of the output. It never becomes the output.

## A pattern that works

- The **media desk computer** owns the projector, the [stage display](/docs/going-live/stage-display) and the livestream feed, and stays on for the whole service.
- A **worship leader or pastor** keeps the schedule open on a phone, adding a scripture or an extra song as the service moves.
- During the sermon, whoever is following along takes passages live while the operator watches the room.

Agree who is taking slides live before the service, not during it.

---

# Help Center: Settings, Shortcuts & Offline

Every keyboard shortcut, every settings page, working without a connection, and installing CoW as an app.

Make Cloud of Worship fit how your church runs. The most used page here is [Keyboard shortcuts](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/keyboard-shortcuts). Keep it open on a Sunday.

## Help Center: Keyboard Shortcuts

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/keyboard-shortcuts

The full shortcut sheet, grouped the same way as in-app: general, slide schedule, live and stage display, and slide styling.

Open the full reference sheet any time by pressing **`?`**, **Cmd/Ctrl + H**, or via the **Shortcuts & Hotkeys** quick action. CoW groups shortcuts the same way in-app, and the tables below match that grouping.

*On Windows and Linux, **Cmd** ("Mod") is **Ctrl**.*

## General

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| **Cmd/Ctrl + K** | Search actions, songs, scriptures, and anything else |
| **`/`** | Jump to the quick actions search |
| **`?`** | Open the shortcuts sheet |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + S** | Open the schedules list |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + ,** | Open app settings |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + P** | Promote the slide you're previewing to the live display |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + Z** | Undo the previous action |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + Y** | Redo the previous action |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + +** | Zoom in / increase display size |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + −** | Zoom out / decrease display size |

## Slide schedule

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| **↓** | Send the next slide in the schedule live |
| **↑** | Send the previous slide in the schedule live |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + 1…9** | Send that numbered slide live |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + 0** | Send the last slide in the schedule live |
| **B** | Blank the live output |

## Live and stage display

*While the Live Display or Stage Display window itself has focus.*

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| **F** | Toggle fullscreen |
| **→** | Go to the next verse (scriptures, songs, hymns) |
| **←** | Go to the previous verse (scriptures, songs, hymns) |

## Slide styling and media

*While a slide is selected in Preview and Edit Content.*

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| **Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + >** | Increase font size |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + <** | Decrease font size |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + U** | Uppercase the slide text |
| **Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + K** | Toggle the line background behind the text |
| **M** | Mute / unmute the media on this slide |
| **Space** | Play / pause the media on this slide |

::callout{type="tip"}
Formatting shortcuts (bold, alignment) work the same whether you're in a text slide's rich-text editor or using the slide toolbar directly: **Cmd/Ctrl + B** for bold, and the usual alignment chords.
::

## Help Center: Settings Reference

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/settings-reference

All ten settings sections: profile, subscription, display, microphone, slides, backgrounds, blank screen, Bible versions, storage and other.

Open settings with **Cmd/Ctrl + ,**, the avatar menu, or the **Open App Settings** quick action. Ten sections:

## Account/Profile Settings
Your profile and, for admins, your church's details.

- **Profile:** a profile photo you can upload, your **Full name** and **Phone number**.
- **Email:** shows whether your address is verified. To change it, enter the **New email** and your **Current password**, click **Send code**, then type the **Code** sent to the new address and click **Confirm email**. **Resend code** is available after a short wait.
- **Church:** the **Church name**, **Pastor**, **Address** and **Church email**. Admins can edit these and upload a church logo, or click **Use default logo** to remove it. Other members see the details but can't change them.

Your plan, subscription status, **Cancel Subscription** and **Billing History** are in Subscription Settings.

## Subscription Settings
Your plan, billing and payment method. If a payment has failed, a banner offers **Retry payment** and **Update payment method**. See [Plans](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/plans-free-vs-teams#if-a-payment-fails). The default **Look and Feel** for new slides: **Default font**, **Default font size** (50–150%), **Default slide alignment**, **Uppercase text**, **Outlined text**, **Bold text**.

## Display Settings
**Control Center** screen info · **Live Window Settings** (Open in fullscreen mode; Close live window when this tab or window is closed; **Let a team member's phone control this output**) · **Secondary Screens** (pick which monitor is the Live display; Refresh screens) · **NDI Live Output** (desktop app only). See [Multi-screen setup](/docs/going-live/multi-screen-setup), [using CoW on your phone](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/using-cloud-of-worship-on-your-phone) and [NDI output](/docs/going-live/ndi-output).

**Let a team member's phone control this output** is on by default and is stored on that computer only. It lets someone on a phone pick this device and take slides live on the screen it is driving, but only while the live window is open here, and you can see who is controlling it above the slide schedule.

## Microphone Settings
**Active Microphone**, **Available Microphones**, **Use as default**. Shows **Microphone access denied** if the browser blocks it.

## Slide Settings
Default font · Default font size · Default lines per slide · **Default line spacing** (Single, Normal or Double) · **Fit each line on one row** (shrinks song and hymn text so each lyric line stays on one row) · Default slide alignment · Default background fill type · Uppercase text · Outlined text · Bold text · Text line background · **Song/hymn title and artistes** (show or hide labels) · **Footnotes and credits** · **Transitions between slides** · **Transition interval** · **Micro animations**

## Slide Background Settings
Default background per slide type: colour, gradient, or image.

## Blank Settings
**Blank Screen**: completely blank by default, or **Use a video / image background** with a **Video** or **Image**.

## Bible Version Settings
**Default Bible version** and **Available Versions**. Use the search box above the list to find a version by name. **Save** a version to make it available offline.

## Storage Settings
**Cloud storage used** against your plan's limit, a breakdown of stored media groups by size, removal options, and **Upload videos to cloud** (on by default; turn it off if you'd rather keep large videos device-local only. Images and audio are unaffected). Destructive actions require typing **"intentionally deleting"** to confirm.

## Other Settings
**Alert Settings** (Default alert limit) · **Content Overlay Layout** (Position and Size) · **Overlays & Themes** (Decorative overlay) · **Transcription Settings** (Automatic transcription actions, Voice Bible version changes)

::callout{type="important" title="Defaults apply to new slides only"}
"Look and Feel" defaults apply to **new slides only**. They do not retroactively restyle existing slides. Edit those individually.
::

---

## Help Center: Offline Use

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/offline-use

Keep presenting when the church Wi-Fi drops. What works offline, what needs a connection, and how to prepare before Sunday.

Church Wi-Fi drops at the worst moments. Cloud of Worship (CoW) is built to keep the service running when it does: your schedule stays on screen, you can keep promoting slides, and anything you change is saved on your device until the connection returns.

## What you'll see when the connection drops

A **"You are offline"** notice appears: *"CoW will save your work until an internet connection returns."* Click **Ok, got it** to dismiss it and carry on. Nothing is lost.

## What keeps working offline

- **Running the service.** The slides already in your schedule, the [Live Display](/docs/going-live/opening-the-live-display) and the arrow keys keep working.
- **Bible verses** for every translation you've saved, and **hymn lookup**. Bibles and hymns are stored in your browser.
- **Songs you've already saved** to your church, and slides in [My Library](/docs/building-your-service/my-library).
- **Creating and editing slides.** New slides and edits are saved on this device and uploaded automatically when you reconnect.
- **Backgrounds and media** that have already been downloaded to this device.

## What needs a connection

- Searching the shared online song lyrics catalogue.
- Backgrounds and media that haven't been downloaded to this device yet. You'll see *"Background is not available offline yet"*.
- YouTube and Vimeo embeds.
- [Sermon transcription](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/sermon-transcription).
- Seeing teammates' changes, and sending yours to them. See [Working as a team](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/working-as-a-team).

## Prepare before the service

1. **Save your Bible translations.** In **Settings → Bible Version Settings**, click **Save** next to each translation you want offline. Saved versions show as **Saved**, with a progress bar while downloading. **KJV, NIV and NKJV** are bundled.
2. **Open the schedule on the media computer while you're online**, and click through any slides with videos or large images so they're downloaded.
3. **Add media ahead of time.** Media uploads in the background, so a large video added just before the service may not be ready. See [Adding media](/docs/building-your-service/adding-media).
4. For the most dependable setup on Windows, use the [desktop app](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/desktop-app) or [install CoW as an app](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/installing-cloud-of-worship).

## After you reconnect

Your changes upload automatically. If something still looks out of date, search the [Quick Actions Pane](/docs/control-center/quick-actions-pane) for:

- **Upload Offline Slides**: pushes slides you made offline to the cloud.
- **Refresh Slides**: pulls in the latest from your team.

Still stuck? See [Sync & team problems](/docs/troubleshooting/sync-and-team-problems).

::callout{type="tip"}
Read more about the offline-first design on the [Offline-first experience](/features/offline-first) page.
::

---

## Help Center: Installing Cloud of Worship as an App

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/installing-cloud-of-worship

Install CoW to your dock, taskbar or home screen as a Progressive Web App, or install the native Windows desktop app.

CoW is a **Progressive Web App**. You can install it to your dock, taskbar or home screen so it opens in its own window without browser chrome.

## To install

Open `app.cloudofworship.com` in Chrome or Edge and use the install icon in the address bar (or **⋮ → Install Cloud of Worship**). On Safari and iOS, use **Share → Add to Home Screen**.

## Two installable apps

| App | Opens at | Use for |
|-----|----------|---------|
| **Cloud of Worship** | `/` | The Control Center |
| **CoW Live** | `/live` | The projection window |

Both open **fullscreen**, which is ideal for the projection machine.

## Or install the native desktop app

On Windows there is also a **native desktop app**. It opens the live and stage windows as real application windows rather than browser popups, detects your monitors without a permission prompt, adds [NDI output](/docs/going-live/ndi-output), and updates itself in the background. Get it from the [download page](/download), or read [the desktop app guide](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/desktop-app) first.

## Updates

When a new version is released, CoW shows an update prompt. You can also visit `/update` and click **Update Cloud of Worship**. Because CoW is a web app, updating is instant. There's nothing to download and reinstall.

The desktop app is different: it downloads new versions quietly in the background and installs them when you restart.

To check which version you are running, open **Settings** and look at the app version at the bottom of the panel, or use the **What's New** quick action to read that version's release notes.

::callout{type="tip"}
See what's changed in each release on the [changelog](/changelog).
::

---

## Help Center: The Desktop App

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/desktop-app

Install Cloud of Worship as a native Windows app for real multi-monitor windows, NDI output and background updates.

*Free feature. Windows only for now.*

Alongside the browser app, Cloud of Worship is available as a **native desktop app**. It is the same product, signed into the same account, working on the same schedules. What it adds is everything a browser is not allowed to do.

## What the desktop app adds

| | Browser | Desktop app |
|---|---------|-------------|
| **Live and stage windows** | Browser popups, subject to popup blockers | Real application windows placed on the monitor you choose |
| **Monitor detection** | Needs browser permission, best in Chrome or Edge | Monitors listed by name, resolution and position, no prompt |
| **[NDI output](/docs/going-live/ndi-output)** | Not available | Available |
| **Updates** | Reload when prompted | Downloaded in the background, applied on restart |

Everything else, every slide type, schedule, setting and shortcut, works identically in both.

## Installing

1. Go to the [download page](/download) and click **Download for Windows**. It always points at the current installer, `Cloud.of.Worship_<version>_x64-setup.exe`.
2. Run the installer, then sign in with your usual account.

If you would rather pick the file yourself, every release is on the [releases page](https://github.com/CoW-Labs/cloudofworship/releases/latest). Take the `-setup.exe`; the `latest.json` and `.sig` files next to it are used by the app's own updater and you do not need them.

Windows may warn that the publisher is not recognised before it will run a newly released installer. Choose **More info → Run anyway**.

Your schedules, songs, library and settings live on your account rather than on the device, so everything you already have appears as soon as you sign in.

::callout{type="important" title="Windows only at the moment"}
The desktop app currently ships for **Windows** only. A macOS build is in progress and is not yet released. Until it is, Mac users should use the browser app, or [install it as a Progressive Web App](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/installing-cloud-of-worship), which is fully supported.
::

## Updates

The desktop app checks for a new version shortly after launch and downloads it quietly in the background. Restarting the app installs it. Nothing interrupts you mid service.

To see which version you are on, open **Settings** and look at the app version at the bottom of the panel. The **What's New** quick action shows the release notes for that version.

## Which should your church use?

**Use the desktop app** if you present from a fixed Windows machine, especially with a second monitor for projection, a stage display for the platform, or a livestream through OBS or vMix.

**Use the browser app** if you present from a Mac, a Chromebook, or a shared computer you cannot install software on.

Both stay in sync. A team member on the desktop app and a team member in a browser tab are working on the same schedule in real time.

---

# Help Center: Troubleshooting

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/troubleshooting

Known behaviours and quick fixes for the live display, sign-in, syncing, media and transcription.

Something not working the way you expect? These pages cover the problems church media teams run into most: a live display that stays black or won't open on the projector, sign-in and verification issues, changes that don't sync between teammates, media that won't upload, and microphone problems with transcription. There's also an honest list of known limitations, so nothing catches you out mid-service.

Can't find your problem here? [Contact support](/contact) and we'll help.

---

## Help Center: Limitations & Known Behaviours

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/troubleshooting/limitations-and-known-behaviours

Honest notes about how CoW behaves in the real world, so nothing surprises you mid-service.

## Performance on low-end devices

On a low-end or heavily loaded machine, the **Control Center** can gradually slow down over a long service, especially with large schedules, lots of media, or many hours of continuous use.

**If that happens, just reload the Control Center** (`app.cloudofworship.com`). **Your Live Display (`app.cloudofworship.com/live`) stays active.** It keeps projecting the whole time you're reloading. The two windows are independent, and when the Control Center comes back it re-reads the current live state from the live window, so you pick up exactly where you left off.

::callout{type="warning" title="Never reload the /live window mid-service"}
That's the one your congregation is looking at. Reload the Control Center instead.
::

::callout{type="important" title="Check this setting first"}
If **Settings → Display Settings → "Close live window when this tab is closed"** is **on**, closing the Control Center tab also kills the projection. Turn it **off** if you want the live window to survive independently.
::

## Both windows must be in the same browser

The Control Center and Live Display talk to each other through the browser itself. Running the Control Center in Chrome and the live window in Safari will **not** work. Open both in the same browser.

## Switching schedules clears the live slide

By design. The Live Display drops to the blank or idle screen and you promote a slide from the new schedule.

## Blank doesn't remember the previous slide

One-way. It clears the live output and won't restore the old slide. It's disabled when nothing is live.

## Style defaults only affect new slides

Changing default font, size or alignment won't restyle slides you already created. Edit those individually.

## Upload size caps

Free: images up to **3 MB**, videos up to **250 MB**, **100 MB** total cloud storage. Teams: **10 MB** images, unlimited video size, **5 GB** storage. Watch your usage in **Settings → Storage Settings**.

## Media uploads in the background

Media is stored locally first and uploaded in the background. Adding a large video right before it's needed is risky. Add media ahead of the service where you can.

## Multi-screen detection is browser-dependent

Automatic screen detection works best in Chrome and Edge. In other browsers you may see **"No external screens detected"** and will need to drag the live window to your projector manually, which works fine.

## Livestream URLs are per-schedule

The copied livestream URL is tied to the active schedule. Switch schedules and you'll need a fresh URL.

## Verification code limits

Three resends maximum, with a two-minute cooldown between them.

## Related guides

- [Live display problems](/docs/troubleshooting/live-display-problems): fixes for the projection window.
- [Offline use](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/offline-use): what works without a connection.
- [Sync & team problems](/docs/troubleshooting/sync-and-team-problems): when changes do not show up.
- [The desktop app](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/desktop-app): native multi-monitor windows on Windows.

---

## Help Center: Live Display Problems

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/troubleshooting/live-display-problems

Sluggish Control Center, a black live window, Go Live not showing a slide, the live window closing, and screens not detected.

## The Control Center feels sluggish

Reload `app.cloudofworship.com`. Your live output keeps running. See [Performance on low-end devices](/docs/troubleshooting/limitations-and-known-behaviours#performance-on-low-end-devices).

## The Live Display says "Select a slide from the Slide Schedule Pane to show here"

Nothing is live. Click a slide in the Slide Schedule Pane.

## My live window is black, or showing a custom video instead of my slide

That's the blank or idle screen. No slide is live. Either **Blank** was clicked or you switched schedules. Click a slide to project it. If you set a video or image in **Settings → Blank Settings**, that plays instead of plain black while idle.

## Clicking "Go Live" didn't put my slide on screen

**Go Live** opens the output *window*. Once open, click a slide in the Slide Schedule Pane to project it, or press **Cmd/Ctrl + P** for the one in the editor. See [Promoting slides](/docs/going-live/promoting-slides).

## The live window closed when I closed my tab

Turn off **Settings → Display Settings → "Close live window when this tab is closed."**

## "No external screens detected"

Click **Refresh screens**. If it persists, your browser may not support screen detection. Chrome and Edge work best. You can always drag the live window to the projector by hand. See [Multi-screen setup](/docs/going-live/multi-screen-setup).

On Windows, the [desktop app](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/desktop-app) reads monitors from the operating system instead of the browser, so this message does not occur there.

## The live window never opened

In a browser, the live display opens as a popup, so a popup blocker can stop it silently. Allow popups for `app.cloudofworship.com` and click **Go Live** again. The [desktop app](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/desktop-app) opens real application windows and is not affected.

## Slides I take live from my phone are not reaching the projector

Check the status row at the top of the **Live** tab on the phone.

- **Not controlling a screen** means you have not picked an output yet. Tap the row and choose one.
- **No output device online** in the list means no computer in your team has a live window open. Open the live display on the projector machine first.
- **Reconnecting to the output…** means the screen you were driving dropped off. Slides are paused until it returns.

Also confirm that **Settings → Display Settings → "Let a team member's phone control this output"** is on at the projector machine. See [using CoW on your phone](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/using-cloud-of-worship-on-your-phone).

---

## Help Center: Account & Sign-in Problems

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/troubleshooting/account-and-sign-in-problems

Email already linked to an account, verification codes not arriving, broken password reset links, and Teams features greyed out.

## "Email linked to an account" during sign-up

That email already has a CoW account. Use **Sign in**, or [reset your password](/docs/getting-started/signing-in-and-password-recovery).

## My verification code isn't arriving

Check spam. A code is sent automatically when you land on the verify page, so you may already have one. **Resend** up to 3 times with a 2-minute wait. If the address was wrong, click it on the verify screen to edit it, and a fresh code goes to the corrected address.

## "This password reset link is missing required information"

The link was incomplete or expired. Click **Request new link** and start over from **Forgot password**.

## Teams features are greyed out after upgrading

Your plan comes from the **church** record. Sign out and back in so CoW re-reads it, or confirm the subscription in **Settings → Account/Profile Settings**. See [Plans: Free vs Teams](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/plans-free-vs-teams).

---

## Help Center: Sync & Team Problems

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/troubleshooting/sync-and-team-problems

Fix the offline banner, teammates' changes not showing up, slides you can't edit, and slides that didn't upload after working offline.

Cloud of Worship (CoW) syncs every change to your church in real time. When something looks out of step between two computers, work through the matching section below.

## "You are offline" banner

CoW has lost its internet connection and is saving your work on this device. Nothing is lost: it uploads automatically when you reconnect. Click **Ok, got it** to dismiss the notice and keep presenting.

If the banner keeps coming back, check the computer's Wi-Fi or network cable. For what does and doesn't work without a connection, see [Offline use](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/offline-use).

## A teammate's changes aren't showing up

1. **Check for the offline banner** on both computers. Changes can't arrive until both are online.
2. **Check you're on the same schedule.** Changes only appear in the schedule they were made in. The schedule name is in the [top bar](/docs/control-center/top-bar-and-live-preview).
3. **Run Refresh Slides.** Search for it in the [Quick Actions Pane](/docs/control-center/quick-actions-pane) to re-fetch every slide from the server.

## Slides I made offline aren't on other computers

Search the Quick Actions Pane for **Upload Offline Slides**. It pushes slides saved on this device up to the cloud. Then run **Refresh Slides** on the other computer.

## A slide won't let me edit it

When you try to edit, you'll see *"Slide is being edited by …"*. Another operator has the slide open, and CoW locks it so two people can't overwrite each other. Wait for them to finish, ask them to move to a different slide, or edit another slide in the meantime. See [Slide locking](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/working-as-a-team#slide-locking).

## A teammate can't see Teams features

Plans belong to the church, not the person. If one operator sees features greyed out, check they joined **your** church through an invite rather than creating a new one. See [Joining an existing church](/docs/getting-started/joining-an-existing-church) and [Plans: Free vs Teams](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/plans-free-vs-teams).

## Still stuck?

[Contact support](/contact) with the name of the schedule and roughly when the problem started, and we'll look into it.

---

## Help Center: Media & Transcription Problems

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/troubleshooting/media-and-transcription-problems

Hymns not found, microphone access denied, and background images or videos that won't upload.

## "Hymn not found" / "We couldn't find that hymn"

Try the hymn **number**, or a distinctive lyric, rather than the full title.

## Microphone access denied (transcription)

Grant microphone permission for `app.cloudofworship.com` in your browser's site settings, then pick your input in **Settings → Microphone Settings**. See [Sermon transcription](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/sermon-transcription).

## My background image or video won't upload

Check the size against your plan's cap. Free allows 3 MB images and 250 MB videos. See [Slide backgrounds](/docs/building-your-service/slide-backgrounds).

## "Some pages didn't upload"

If the connection drops while you import a PDF or add images, CoW keeps the files on your computer and tells you how many pages didn't reach the cloud. They still show on your screen, but not on other devices or for your team yet. CoW retries in the background, and again when the connection comes back or the schedule is next opened, so you don't need to add them again.

## Transcription stopped: "Your free minutes are used"

Free churches get 10 transcription minutes once. On Teams the limit is 3 hours a week, plus whatever you didn't use the week before, and it resets every Monday. See [Sermon transcription](/docs/teams-and-collaboration/sermon-transcription#how-much-you-can-transcribe).

---

# Help Center: Post Mortems

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/post-mortems

What went wrong, how we fixed it, and what we changed so it does not happen again.

When something goes wrong with Cloud of Worship, we write it up here: what happened, who was affected, how we fixed it, and what we changed so it doesn't happen again. We publish these because churches rely on us every week and deserve to know what happened.

For problems on your own setup, see [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting).

---

## Help Center: Media and Bible downloads, October 2026

URL: https://cloudofworship.com/docs/post-mortems/media-and-bible-downloads-october-2026

Why some media and Bible translations would not download from 11 October 2026, and how everything was restored by 22 October 2026.

::callout{type="success" title="Resolved"}
Everything is back as of 22 October 2026. All 38 Bible translations, all preset background videos, and the images and videos you uploaded before the incident are available to every church again.
::

## Summary

Since around 11 October 2026, some files stored in Cloud of Worship could not be downloaded. This mostly affected uploaded images and videos, background videos, and some Bible translations.

Your schedules, slides, songs, lyrics and settings were never affected, and no data has been lost. Everything is still safely stored.

## What you may have noticed

- Images or videos you uploaded did not show on a new computer, or showed a loading state.
- Some Bible translations would not download.
- Background videos did not load on first use.
- Uploading new media failed or kept retrying.

If your media was already saved on your computer before the incident, it kept working as normal.

## Why it happened

We store media files with Amazon Web Services (AWS). A billing issue on our account led AWS to suspend it, which locked access to the stored files.

We resolved the billing issue, but AWS was slow to reopen the account because we are not on a premium support plan, which gets faster replies. This was a mistake on our side, not something any church did.

## Timeline

| Date | What happened |
|------|---------------|
| 22 October | Media uploaded before the incident restored and available to all customers. Everything is back. |
| 17 October | The remaining 19 Bible translations restored, including MSG, TPT, WEB and the non-English Bibles. All 38 translations now work. |
| 13 October | New storage provider set up. 19 Bible translations and all background videos moved to it. New uploads are being switched over. |
| 11 to 13 October | Billing issue resolved and support case opened with AWS. Still waiting on a response. |
| Around 11 October | AWS suspended our account. Media downloads and uploads began to fail. |

## What we have done so far

- **Bible translations:** all 38 translations work again. 19 came back on 13 October, including KJV, NIV, NKJV, ESV, NLT, AMP and the Nigerian language Bibles. The other 19, including MSG, TPT, WEB and the non-English Bibles, were rebuilt from public sources and checked against second copies on 17 October.
- **Background videos:** the six preset background videos work again.
- **New storage:** we set up a second storage provider, Cloudflare, so new uploads no longer depend on AWS.
- **Smarter loading:** the app now checks the new storage first and falls back to the old location, so files start working as soon as we move them.
- **Older uploads:** on 22 October, images and videos uploaded before the incident were restored and are now available to all customers.
- **AWS:** we resolved the billing issue and pressed AWS to reopen the account.

## What is still left

Nothing. All media and Bible translations are available again.

## What to do now

- You do not need to do anything. Media that looked missing or stuck loading should now appear on its own.
- If a file you need is still missing, write to us at the address below and we will look into it straight away.

## What we are changing

- **Billing:** we are adding a backup payment method and reminders so a billing issue cannot interrupt service again.
- **Backups:** media will be kept with more than one provider, so one account problem cannot lock your files.

We are sorry. Sunday services depend on Cloud of Worship, and this should not have happened.

If something is still not working for your church, write to [hello@cloudofworship.com](mailto:hello@cloudofworship.com).

## Related guides

- [Offline use](/docs/settings-and-shortcuts/offline-use): save Bible versions so they work without a connection.
- [Media & transcription problems](/docs/troubleshooting/media-and-transcription-problems): fixes for media that will not load.
- [Adding media](/docs/building-your-service/adding-media): add media ahead of the service.

---
